talking.motion: Locked-off camera, high angle over the round pub table. The young man in the dark navy hoodie, seated at the right edge, keeps his head low toward the sheet and, about half a second in, whispers fast, lips making small, clear shapes. Once the line ends his lips close and he holds still. The other three men hold almost still. He whispers: A hundred million? That's loads.

Fixed camera. The bearded man in the plaster-flecked camouflage jacket, bent over the answer sheet with the pencil in his hand, whispers quickly under his breath from about half a second in, lips shaping every word. When the line ends he shuts his mouth and holds still. The man behind him stays put. He whispers: More. I've done three of them B&B jobs for the council this year. Every room, every night.

Static camera. The young man in the dark navy hoodie, pen on the beer mat, keeps his head down and, about half a second in, whispers rapidly, lips working small and quick. Once the line is done his mouth closes and he holds still, eyes on the mat. The man in the foreground does not move. He whispers: Say fifty quid a night. I don't know how much things are,

Static camera. The young man in the dark navy hoodie, pen on the beer mat, keeps his head down and, about half a second in, whispers rapidly, lips working small and quick. Once the line is done his mouth closes and he holds still, eyes on the mat. The man in the foreground does not move. He whispers: I only buy CBD ramen suppositories. Every night. A hundred thousand rooms?

Fixed camera. The bearded man in the plaster-spattered camouflage jacket, seated at left in profile, keeps his eyes on the red-bearded man in the denim jacket facing him and, about half a second in, whispers sharply and fast through barely parted lips. When the line ends his mouth shuts and he holds still. The red-bearded man and the grey-haired woman stay still. He whispers: Fuck off, get your own answers.

Locked camera. The man in the dark suit and loosened tie keeps his eyes down on the pint in his hand, never looking up, and about half a second in whispers quickly, dry and offhand, lips moving crisply. After the line his mouth closes and he holds still. The shoulder in the foreground does not move. He whispers: Paying by the night is the dearest way to buy anything.

Locked camera. The man in the dark suit and loosened tie keeps his eyes down on the pint in his hand, never looking up, and about half a second in whispers quickly, dry and scornful, lips moving crisply. After the line his mouth closes and he holds still. The shoulder in the foreground does not move. He whispers: It's billions with a B. Keep up, you morons.

Static camera. The young man in the dark navy hoodie at the centre, hands open in a puzzled shrug, looks at the man in the suit and, about half a second in, whispers quickly, lips clear. When the line ends he closes his mouth and holds still, hands where they are. The man in the suit and the man in the foreground hold almost still. He whispers: So they rent the same rooms every year? Why don't they just own them?

Fixed camera. The bearded man in the plaster-flecked camouflage jacket, bent over the answer sheet with the pencil in his hand, whispers quickly under his breath from about half a second in, lips shaping every word. When the line ends he shuts his mouth and holds still. The man behind him stays put. He whispers: Every year. And at the end nobody owns a single brick.

Static camera. The man in the suit on the right, pint in hand, looks at the young man in the hoodie and, about half a second in, whispers flatly and briskly, lips moving clearly. When the line ends his mouth closes and he holds still. The young man and the man in the foreground hold almost still. He whispers: So buy the bricks.

stills.prompt:
Use his face from the portrait, and the room, the round table and the three other men from the pub photo. Vertical 9:16 medium close-up at the table: the older man in the olive waterproof jacket, short grey hair, white stubble, ruddy cheeks, his face about a third of the frame, lit by a direct on-camera flash. On the table in front of him lie the answer sheet, covered in faint unreadable pencil marks, and a short pencil. He has just raised his eyes from the sheet to the others across the table, mouth closed, calm and sure. The others sit out of focus at the frame edge. Dark wood panelling behind.
Thanks.

Use his face, hair and clothes from the portrait, and the bar from the pub photo. Vertical 9:16 medium shot at the dark wooden bar, on-camera flash. The same sixty-three-year-old regular: thin sandy-grey comb-over, bushy grey eyebrows, big ears, red bulbous nose, grey stubble, brown corduroy jacket, mustard knitted tank top over a checked shirt. He sits on a green leather stool, asleep, elbow on the bar, cheek pushed up against his palm, eyes shut, mouth hanging open. A half-drunk pint stands by his elbow. Unposed and real, a tired man dozing. Bottles behind soft, their labels blank.
Thanks.

Use the bar and its warm light from the pub photo. Vertical 9:16 product shot. One clear, straight-sided pint glass, empty and upright, stands dead centre on the dark polished wood bar, filling the middle of the frame, seen front-on from the glass's own height. A brass beer tap sits just above and behind it. The glass is spotless and completely plain all the way round, smooth bare glass. Shallow depth of field: the pub behind melts into warm amber blur. Pump badges plain and blank. Clean, still, crisp.
Thanks.

motions.motion: Fixed camera. The older man in the olive waterproof jacket, eyes on the others, whispers quietly and briskly from about half a second in, calm and certain, lips moving small but clear. When the line ends his mouth closes and he holds still, gaze steady. The blurred figures at the edge barely move. He whispers: I know literally no one who's been in them.

Fixed camera. The man asleep at the bar stays asleep throughout. In the first two seconds his cheek slowly slips off his palm, his head sags and drops onto the bar top with a small, dull thunk beside his pint, his arm sliding flat. Then he lies there, mouth open, breathing faintly; nothing else moves. The pint stays put. Real, small, heavy movement.
Thanks.

Locked-off camera, no movement at all. The pint glass stays fixed dead centre, never moving, turning, tilting or changing shape. Beer runs from the tap in a steady amber stream into the glass; over about six seconds the level rises, bubbles climbing, until it is full to the top with a clean, tight white head. Then the stream stops and everything is still. The pub behind stays soft and warm.
Thanks.
